candidates.title: iPhone 18 Pro vs Pixel 11 Pro: How Apple and Google's flagships stack up
candidates.description: Google and Apple's latest flagships feature more AI, better cameras and few reasons to switch ecosystems.
candidates.body_text: More AI, better cameras and few reasons to switch ecosystems. Apple / Google / Will Shanklin for Engadget Add Engadget on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover The iPhone 18 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro are the latest examples of a familiar story: Apple and Google refining, rather than reinventing, mature flagship smartphones. Both are expensive, powerful phones with top-notch screens, three rear cameras and (like it or not) an ever-growing list of AI features. They both come in two sizes and have similar price tags. There are still plenty of subtle differences. But neither phone likely gives you a compelling reason to switch ecosystems. If you're happy with how your iPhone plays nicely with your MacBook, iPad, Apple Watch and AirPods, there's no reason to jump ship to Android. Ditto for the Pixel if you're invested in Google's devices and services. While the ecosystem question is easy, there's still plenty to learn from the details. Let's line them up and see where they differ. Apple / Google / Will Shanklin for Engadget Design-wise, both phones (mostly) stay the course. The Pixel keeps its signature full-width camera bar, but adds edge-to-edge glass for a more seamless look. Its aluminum frame matches the phone's color, whether you go with Canyon, Fog, Olive or Obsidian. The Pixel also has an easy-to-overlook improvement: the new camera bar keeps the phone more stable and balanced on a table. candidates.description: Oracle to spend $700 million more on restructuring costs as it ramps up AI spending    CNA
candidates.body_text: Business Oracle to spend $700 million more on restructuring costs as it ramps up AI spending FILE PHOTO: Oracle logo is seen in this illustration created on September 9, 2025. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo 11 Sep 2026 05:01PM (Updated: 12 Sep 2026 07:47AM) Bookmark WhatsApp Telegram Facebook Twitter Email LinkedIn Set CNA as your preferred source on Google Add CNA as a trusted source to help Google better understand and surface our content in search results. Sept 11 : Oracle said restructuring costs, part of a plan that includes job cuts, will rise about $700 million as the cloud company seeks to rein in costs while spending billions to capitalize on booming demand for artificial intelligence services. In a regulatory filing on Friday, Oracle said the increase, disclosed after the end of its August quarter, raises the expected cost of its fiscal 2026 restructuring plan to roughly $2.8 billion. The plan, which the company says includes severance, contract terminations and other exit expenses, is partly tied to the adoption of AI across some functions. The cuts come as Oracle navigates a volatile stretch for its stock, with investors seemingly split between confidence in its AI-driven growth and concern over how it is funding that growth. Oracle's shares rose as much as 7.8 per cent on Friday after a $26 billion increase in its revenue backlog eased some concerns about its debt-fueled spending spree. candidates.title: New images show a detailed view of Meta's upcoming mixed reality headset
candidates.description: The device known as Project Phoenix is a new form factor for Meta.
candidates.body_text: The device known as Project Phoenix is a new form factor for Meta. Meta (via UploadVR) Add Engadget on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Meta appears to have unintentionally shown off its upcoming mixed reality headset a bit ahead of schedule. Images of the device, which has been known as "Project Phoenix", have surfaced and they provide a fairly detailed look at the lightweight headset. The images were originally published by UploadVR , which found the files in a HorizonOS app Meta released called "HorizonOS Prescription Lens." The app, which has since been removed, seems to be intended for people who need prescription inserts for the device. But while Meta seems to have released the app as a kind of "placeholder," UploadVR found that it included image files that clearly show the headset from different angles. The images seem to match what we have heard about the mixed reality device for more than a year . "Phoenix" is a different form factor than other Quest-branded hardware we've seen from Meta. It looks more similar to glasses-like devices like Xreal's Aura headse t. And one of the images clearly shows a cable, which lines up with previous rumors that Phoenix will rely on a tethered connection to a separate puck. One view we can't see in the new images is what the headset looks like from the front, so there are still some details we don't have.
